q: A stores procurement tender has an estimated cost of Rs 80 lakh. Applying ACS No. 11, what Bid Security must a normal bidder submit?

options.A: Rs 4,00,000, being 5% of the estimated cost
options.B: A slab-based amount varying with the estimated cost
options.C: Rs 80,000, being 1% of the estimated cost
options.D: Rs 1,60,000, being a flat 2% of the estimated cost

e: ACS-11 fixes Bid Security at a flat 2% of estimated cost for all cases; the old slab formula no longer applies.

q: In a procurement contract of Rs 5 crore, the contractor proposes to sub-contract work worth Rs 2.50 crore. What is the correct position after ACS No. 11?

options.A: The proposal is not permissible, as sub-contracting is capped at 40% of the contract price, i.e. Rs 2 crore in this case
options.B: The proposal is permissible, as sub-contracting up to 50% is allowed
options.C: The proposal is permissible, as there is no cap on sub-contracting
options.D: The proposal is not permissible, as sub-contracting is capped at 25% of the contract price

e: ACS-11 caps sub-contracting at a maximum of 40% of the contract price.

q: A bidder in a procurement tender quotes 8% below the advertised value and becomes the successful bidder. What Additional Performance Guarantee (APG) is required under ACS No. 11?

options.A: No APG is required for any low bid
options.B: APG of 2% is required, equal to the Bid Security rate
options.C: APG of 10% is required for every bid below the advertised value
options.D: APG of 5% is required, because the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value

e: Under ACS-11, APG of 5% applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.

q: A successful bidder has quoted 3% below the advertised value in a procurement tender governed by ACS No. 11. The tender authority demands an Additional Performance Guarantee. What is the correct position?

options.A: APG of 5% is payable for every bid below the advertised value
options.B: APG of 3% is payable, matching the percentage below the advertised value
options.C: No APG is payable, because a bid 0% to 5% below the advertised value attracts no additional security
options.D: APG of 2% is payable as Bid Security

e: ACS-11 provides no additional security where the bid is 0% to 5% below the advertised value.

q: For a procurement tender, a bidder argues that the Bid Capacity check does not apply because the earlier Rs 20 crore threshold has not been crossed, although the tender exceeds Rs 10 crore. What is the position after ACS No. 11?

options.A: The argument fails, because the Bid Capacity eligibility threshold has been reduced from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore
options.B: The argument succeeds, because the threshold remains Rs 20 crore
options.C: The argument succeeds, because Bid Capacity has been abolished by ACS-11
options.D: The argument fails, because the threshold has been reduced to Rs 5 crore

e: ACS-11 lowered the Bid Capacity eligibility threshold from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.

q: During a procurement tender, a bidder is found to have violated the expanded Code of Integrity introduced under ACS No. 11. Which consequence can follow?

options.A: Only recovery of Bid Security, with no debarment possible
options.B: Forfeiture and debarment, with a reference to the CCI where applicable, as provided in the expanded Code of Integrity
options.C: Automatic award of the contract to the violating bidder
options.D: Only a verbal warning, with no other consequence

e: ACS-11 expanded the Code of Integrity with forfeiture, debarment and CCI reference as consequences of violation.

q: A start-up recognised by DIPP participates in a stores procurement tender after ACS No. 11 and claims exemption from Bid Security. How should the claim be treated?

options.A: The claim is invalid; start-ups must pay double Bid Security
options.B: The claim is valid; DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from Bid Security
options.C: The claim is valid only if the start-up pays 50% Bid Security
options.D: The claim is invalid; no category is exempt from Bid Security

e: Start-ups recognised by DIPP are exempt from Bid Security, while Labour Cooperative Societies submit only 50%.

q: A Labour Cooperative Society bids in a procurement tender where the normal Bid Security works out to Rs 2,00,000. How much Bid Security must the society submit after ACS No. 11?

options.A: Rs 2,00,000, with no concession
options.B: Rs 50,000, being 25% of the normal Bid Security
options.C: Nil, because Labour Cooperative Societies are fully exempt
options.D: Rs 1,00,000, being 50% of the normal Bid Security

e: Labour Cooperative Societies submit only 50% of the Bid Security; full exemption is for DIPP-recognised start-ups.

q: A contractor holding a procurement contract of Rs 10 crore sub-contracts a portion worth Rs 3.50 crore and seeks approval. What is the correct assessment under ACS No. 11?

options.A: It exceeds the limit, as the cap is 30% of the contract price
options.B: It exceeds the limit, as sub-contracting is not permitted at all
options.C: It is within the limit, as Rs 3.50 crore is 35% and the cap is 40% of the contract price
options.D: It is within the limit, as the cap is 50% of the contract price

e: Sub-contracting up to 40% of the contract price is permitted under ACS-11.

q: A successful bidder quotes exactly 5% below the advertised value. The accounts branch asks whether a 5% APG must be taken. What is the correct advice under ACS No. 11?

options.A: No APG is required, because APG applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value
options.B: APG of 5% is required at exactly 5% below as well
options.C: APG of 2.5% is required at exactly 5% below
options.D: APG is required only if the bidder is a start-up

e: The APG trigger is strictly more than 5% below; the 0% to 5% band attracts no additional security.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bid Security under ACS-11 is a flat 2% of the estimated cost.
2. Bid Security continues to be calculated on the old threshold-based slab formula.
3. Bid Security is rounded off to the nearest Rs 100.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 and 3 only
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 2 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. ACS-11 replaced the old formula with a flat 2%, rounded to the nearest Rs 100.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sub-contracting is capped at 40% of the contract price under ACS-11.
2. A contractor may sub-contract up to 60% of the contract price.
3. The sub-contracting cap was introduced by ACS-11.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 1 and 3 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: The cap is 40%, not 60%. Statements 1 and 3 correctly state the ACS-11 position.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bid Capacity eligibility threshold has been reduced from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.
2. The Bid Capacity threshold has been raised from Rs 10 crore to Rs 20 crore.
3. The threshold change was made by ACS-11.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1 and 2 only

e: ACS-11 reduced, and did not raise, the threshold from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. APG of 5% is required where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.
2. APG is required even where the bid is 2% below the advertised value.
3. A bid 0% to 5% below the advertised value attracts no additional security.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 3
options.D: 1 and 3 only

e: Statements 1 and 3 state the ACS-11 APG structure; statement 2 contradicts the 0-5% no-APG band.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from Bid Security.
2. Labour Cooperative Societies submit only 50% of the Bid Security.
3. Labour Cooperative Societies are fully exempt from Bid Security.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 and 3 only
options.B: 1 and 3 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 3
options.D: 1 and 2 only

e: Full exemption is for DIPP start-ups; Labour Cooperative Societies get a 50% concession, not full exemption.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. EMD is now known as Bid Security.
2. Performance Guarantee remains 5% under the ACS-11 position.
3. Bid Security and Performance Guarantee are both fixed at 2%.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 and 3 only
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 2 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: EMD is renamed Bid Security at 2%; PG stays at 5%, so statement 3 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. ACS-11 expanded the Code of Integrity.
2. Violation of the Code of Integrity can lead to forfeiture and debarment.
3. The expanded Code makes no reference to the CCI.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: The expanded Code of Integrity carries forfeiture and debarment consequences with a CCI reference, so statement 3 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bid Security is 2% of the estimated cost of the work.
2. The Performance Guarantee is to be submitted within 21 days.
3. No penal interest applies for delay in submitting the Performance Guarantee.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 and 3 only
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 3
options.D: 1 and 3 only

e: PG is 5% within 21 days, with 12% penal interest from the 22nd day for delay, so statement 3 is wrong.

q: What is the rate of Bid Security fixed by ACS No. 11?

options.A: 1% of the estimated cost of the work
options.B: 2% of the estimated cost of the work
options.C: 5% of the estimated cost of the work
options.D: A slab rate depending on the estimated cost

e: ACS-11 fixed Bid Security at a flat 2% of the estimated cost, replacing the old formula.

q: What is the maximum sub-contracting permitted under ACS No. 11, as a percentage of the contract price?

options.A: 25% of the contract price
options.B: 50% of the contract price
options.C: 60% of the contract price
options.D: 40% of the contract price

e: Sub-contracting is limited to a maximum of 40% of the contract price.

q: After ACS No. 11, the Bid Capacity eligibility threshold stands at:

options.A: Rs 20 crore, unchanged
options.B: Rs 5 crore, reduced from Rs 20 crore
options.C: Rs 10 crore, reduced from Rs 20 crore
options.D: Rs 25 crore, raised from Rs 20 crore

e: ACS-11 reduced the Bid Capacity eligibility threshold from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.

q: Under ACS No. 11, an Additional Performance Guarantee of 5% is required when the bid is:

options.A: More than 5% below the advertised value
options.B: At or above the advertised value
options.C: Up to 5% below the advertised value
options.D: Exactly at the advertised value

e: APG of 5% applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.

q: Bid Security under ACS-11 is to be rounded off to the nearest:

options.A: Rs 100
options.B: Rs 10
options.D: Rs 500

e: Bid Security is rounded off to the nearest Rs 100.

q: Which of the following statements about the Code of Integrity introduced under ACS No. 11 is NOT correct?

options.A: A breach of the Code of Integrity can lead to forfeiture of earnest money or security deposit
options.B: A bidder found in breach of the Code may be debarred from participating in future tenders
options.C: Suspected cartelisation amounting to a breach of the Code can be referred to the Competition Commission of India
options.D: A bidder who breaches the Code of Integrity faces no consequence beyond a written warning

e: ACS No. 11 gives the Code of Integrity real teeth: forfeiture of earnest money/security, debarment from future tenders and reference of suspected cartelisation to the CCI. A mere warning with no other consequence is not the position.

q: Which of the following is NOT correct in respect of Bid Security after ACS No. 11?

options.A: DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from Bid Security
options.B: Labour Cooperative Societies are exempt from the entire Bid Security
options.C: Bid Security is 2% of the estimated cost
options.D: Bid Security is rounded off to the nearest Rs 100

e: Labour Cooperative Societies submit 50% of Bid Security; they are not fully exempt.

q: Which statement about the Additional Performance Guarantee under ACS No. 11 is NOT correct?

options.A: APG of 5% is payable where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value
options.B: The APG test is applied with reference to the advertised value
options.C: APG of 5% is payable even if the bid is only 1% below the advertised value
options.D: No APG is payable for a bid 0% to 5% below the advertised value

e: A bid 1% below falls in the 0-5% band and attracts no APG.

q: Which of the following is NOT a change brought by ACS No. 11?

options.A: Bid Security has been fixed at 2% of the estimated cost
options.B: Sub-contracting has been capped at 40% of the contract price
options.C: Bid Capacity threshold has been reduced to Rs 10 crore
options.D: Performance Guarantee has been raised from 5% to 10%

e: PG stays at 5%; ACS-11 did not raise it to 10%. The other three are genuine ACS-11 changes.

q:
Assertion (A): A bid 7% below the advertised value attracts an Additional Performance Guarantee of 5% under ACS No. 11.
Reason (R): APG applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.B: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.C: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both are true, and R correctly explains A because 7% below crosses the more-than-5% trigger.

q:
Assertion (A): A DIPP-recognised start-up must submit full Bid Security in a procurement tender.
Reason (R): DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from Bid Security under ACS No. 11.

options.A: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.C: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.D: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

e: A is false because such start-ups are exempt; R is true and states that exemption.

q:
Assertion (A): Sub-contracting beyond 40% of the contract price is not permitted under ACS No. 11.
Reason (R): Bid Security is fixed at 2% of the estimated cost under ACS No. 11.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.C: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both statements are true, but the Bid Security rate does not explain the sub-contracting cap.
